message.content:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, symmetric enlargement of the hilar lymph nodes with well-defined margins and clear lung fields (no parenchymal opacities), which is the classic radiographic presentation of Stage I sarcoidosis. This symmetry and lack of pulmonary infiltrates help distinguish it from malignancy (often asymmetric/irregular), tuberculosis (often unilateral/calcified), or infectious processes (associated with opacities).
